reason: Wording: archive.org full-text search reaches the Columbia 1967 volume itself, in two scans (bwb_W9-BRV-171 and essaysinidleness0000yosh). Both give the section 7 text, carrying Keene's footnote markers after Adashino and Toribeyama, as: but lingered on forever in the world, how things would lose. The same volume also contains a second occurrence reading in this world. That comes from Keene's own Introduction, where he quotes the passage, and it is the source of the in this world variant on Wikipedia and in The Pleasures of Japanese Literature (1988). Keene's essays in Landscapes and Portraits (1971) and Appreciations of Japanese Culture (1981) quote it as in the world and footnote it Kenko, p. 7. The book's index gives Toribeyama, 7. So the verifier's correction is right for section 7. Its note should add that Keene's Introduction quotes the sentence with this world, which explains the variant; the note as written implies the Columbia volume was checked, and the verifier did not open it. Page 7 is established, so the source can carry it (betterCitation). Attribution: Kenkō's, not on the misattribution list. shipped.js: not shipped, no near opening, Kenkō 2 of 3 (months 3 and 10), not banned, so this would be his third.
